items.title: Amazfit’s stylish budget tracker is nearly matching its best price to date
items.raw:
The Amazfit Active 2 is a solid fitness tracker that could easily be mistaken for a smartwatch. | Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge	

Amazfit might not have the name recognition of a company like Garmin or Fitbit, but its wearables consistently impress, with the Amazfit Active 2 being one of the best fitness trackers you can buy. And right now, it’s on sale for just $84.99 ($15 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and Target, which is only $5 more than its best price to date.
Amazfit Active 2

Where to Buy:

 $99.99 $84.99 at Amazon
 $99.99 $84.99 at Best Buy
 $99.99 $84.99 at Target

Even at its regular price of $99.99, Amazfit’s feature-packed wearable is an incredible value. Its bright, 2,000-nit OLED display and handsome stainless steel case give it the look of a stylish everyday watch, rather than a basic fitness tracker. The platform-agnostic wearable also supports 160 different sport types and an array of core health features, including continuous heart rate and blood oxygen monitoring, as well as menstrual cycle, skin temperature, and stress tracking. It’s also well-suited for outdoor workouts thanks to its support for offline maps and turn-by-turn navigation, which is backed by accurate location tracking across all five major GNSS satellite systems.
Battery life is another area where it shines. In our testing, the Active 2 also lasted around eight or nine days on a single charge, easily besting more advanced smartwatches. It’s even equipped with an AI-powered coach that can generate personalized training plans, along with an on-device voice assistant for hands-free control.
Read our full Amazfit Active 2 review.

items.title: Some of our favorite 4K UHD Blu-rays are three for $33 at Amazon right now
items.raw:
The holidays — and the copious amounts of binge-watching that come with them — are very much behind us at this point, but that doesn’t mean there won’t be time to catch up on the movies from last year (and beyond) you might have missed. Thankfully, Amazon has brought back one of the better promos we’ve seen in recent years, allowing you to snag three 4K UHD Blu-ray discs for $33 through January 19th.
It should go without saying that you’ll need a 4K Blu-ray player like Panasonic’s UB820-K or step-down DP-UB420-K to take full advantage of the discs; however, a disc-based Xbox Series X or PS5 will also work just fine, even if they’re not quite as capable when it comes to features as a dedicated option. As for the promo, Amazon’s discounted catalog includes more than 150 Blu-ray titles, including newer films like F1 The Movie, Wicked, and James Gunn’s latest Superman entry. A few more midweek discounts
Genki’s excellent Mooonbase charger has once again fallen to $89.99 ($50 off) at Amazon in blue and orange, matching its lowest price to date. The retrofuturism-inspired power strip features three AC plugs (1,250W max power) and four USB-C ports, which can output up to 240W of total power. That said, I’d argue the bigger draw is that each AC outlet features a handsome, transparent design with color LEDs that you can cycle through with a push of a button. Just don’t forget to grab some USB-C cables to go with it.
If you own a Nintendo Switch 2, Tomtoc’s FancyCase-G05 Slim Case is currently on sale at Amazon and B&H Photo for an all-time low of $24.99 ($12 off) in various colors. Of all the cases we’ve tested for Nintendo’s latest console thus far, the G05 remains our favorite zip-up model, as it’s more rigid than competing models from PowerA / Belkin and offers ample vertical clearance above the Joy-Con 2’s analog sticks; it also holds up to 12 game cartridges.
Not everything announced at CES 2026 is slated to arrive in the latter half of the year. Case in point? Satechi’s new Thunderbolt 5 CubeDock, which is available for preorder from Satechi ahead of its Q1 debut for $319.99 ($80 off) when you use coupon code CES2026 for 20 percent off. The promising, Mac Mini-esque hub offers an NVMe SSD enclosure and an array of ports in a relatively small footprint, including three Thunderbolt 5 downstream ports with up to 120Gbps speeds, 10Gbps USB-C and USB-A ports, UHS-II SD and microSD card slots, and a 2.5Gb ethernet port.

items.title: Yemen separatist leader to make last stand after rejecting Saudi ultimatum, supporters say

Saudi airstrikes hit Aidarous al-Zubaidi’s military camps after he defies a demand to travel to Riyadh for talks
The leader of Yemen’s routed southern separatist movement, Aidarous al-Zubaidi, has decided to make a defiant last stand in Aden, his supporters say, rejecting a Saudi ultimatum to travel to Riyadh for talks and – for now – a plan to flee the southern capital.
Al-Zubaidi, the president of the Southern Transitional Council (STC), has been gathering his remaining troops in Aden as rival Saudi-backed forces seek to take control of Aden. His supporters said his mood was to fight it out although he knew it was likely there would be an attempt to kill him.

items.title: Weather tracker: Arctic air grips Europe as severe winds batter Corsica
items.raw:
Subzero temperatures, heavy snowfall and powerful gusts mark a harsh start to 2026 for many
It has been a cold start to the year across much of Europe, particularly in central regions, where temperatures dropped to double-digit negatives. Heavy snowfall hit parts of eastern and central Europe on New Year’s Eve, notably in Poland and Ukraine, with similar conditions across the Alps on the first few days of the year.
The cold is likely to continue this week as an Arctic air mass sinks south across Europe, pulling temperatures well below the seasonal average outside south-east Europe. Temperatures are expected to fall widely by about 5C (41F) below average, with some areas – such as parts of central and north-eastern Europe – up to 10C lower than the norm. When wind chill is taken into account, it will feel even colder.

items.title: Cremation pyre in Africa thought to be world’s oldest containing adult remains
items.raw:
9,500-year-old pyre uncovered in Malawi offers rare insight into rituals of ancient African hunter-gatherer groups
A cremation pyre built about 9,500 years ago has been discovered in Africa, offering a fresh glimpse into the complexity of ancient hunter-gatherer communities.
Researchers say the pyre, discovered in a rock shelter at the foot of Mount Hora in northern Malawi, is thought to be the oldest in the world to contain adult remains, the oldest confirmed intentional cremation in Africa, and the first pyre to be associated with African hunter-gatherers.

items.title: US ‘adapt, shrink or die’ terms for $2bn aid pot will mean UN bowing down to Washington, say experts

The $2bn (£1.5bn) of aid the US pledged this week may have been hailed as “bold and ambitious” by the UN but could be the “nail in the coffin” in changing to a shrunken, less flexible aid system dominated by Washington’s political priorities, aid experts fear.
After a year of deep cuts in aid budgets by the US and European countries, the announcement of new money for the humanitarian system is a source of some relief, but experts are deeply concerned about demands that the US has imposed on how the money should be managed and where it can go.

items.title: Tensions between Saudis and Emiratis over future of Yemen reach boiling point
items.raw:
Dispute has potential to create civil war in south of Yemen and spill over into neighbouring countries
Tensions between the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia over the future of Yemen and the imminent possibility of the declaration of an independent southern state have reached boiling point with Saudi Arabia in effect accusing the UAE of threatening its future security.
The dispute has the potential to create a civil war within the south of Yemen and also spill over into other disputes including in Sudan and the Horn of Africa where the two countries often find themselves backing opposite sides. Yemen could yet become only one theatre in which the two vastly wealthy Gulf states vie for political influence, control of shipping lanes and commercial access.
